questions.question: When the model emits several tool_use requests at once, who decides whether they run in parallel or in series?
options: The model: it fixes the execution mode while generating the requests
The client: the model only lays the requests out, and how they run is the client's scheduling problem
The downstream service: its concurrency ceiling decides automatically
The API gateway: requests always queue in the order they arrive
questions.explanation: See the "Several requests in one reply" section: the decision to parallelize or not is not the model's — it only lays the requests out at once, and how they run is the client's scheduling problem.

questions.question: What is the single criterion for deciding whether a batch of requests may run in parallel?
options: Whether the requests appear in one model reply
Whether the requests call the same tool function
Whether a later request needs an earlier request's result to build its parameters
Whether the batch contains more than two requests
questions.explanation: See the "Only the independent may run in parallel" section: the criterion is one line — does a later request need an earlier request's result; parallelizing dependent requests makes the error propagate silently downstream.

questions.question: Running concurrently, result #2 arrives before #1. What should the client do?
options: Reply with #2 right away so the model can start reasoning early
Buffer each result under its tool_use_id and reply only when all have arrived
Discard #2 and reply with #1 alone, letting the model wait for the next round
Abort the whole batch and re-run the requests serially
questions.explanation: See the "Pairing the replies by id" section: completion order is uncontrollable, so the client buffers each result under its tool_use_id and replies only when all have arrived — a partial reply lets the model answer on incomplete observations.
